schema.fact_or_item: a supplied fact, a record list (earnings, receipts, holdings), the relationships, or a derived item
schema.kind: fact | record | relationship | agency record | application data | rule | figure
schema.settles: deny: an answer can settle not eligible; approve: an answer can settle eligible early; both
schema.conditions: the necessary condition(s) of the outcome the question decides, with the paragraph
schema.programs_served: program families whose outcomes read it (docs/reviews/cross-program-primitives.json read_by_programs)
schema.denial_share: share of stored deny answers of this program whose minimal denial set holds it: with the current engine, and with a three-valued (possible-values) case
schema.cost: applicant burden: 0.5 application data or agency record, 1 yes/no or plain choice, 2 a date or the relationship grid, 3 an amount to look up or a status in statute vocabulary, 4 dated income records, 5 resource records
schema.needs_verification: the verification element the answer falls under, or null
schema.skips: fields that become irrelevant once the answer is known

branches: No child under 13 (or under 19 with additional care needs): skip every CCCAP question
No child under 19: skip SUN Bucks unless a younger child is enrolled in school; CHP+ only for a pregnant person (step 2)
No child under 18 (or 18 in secondary school) and no one pregnant (step 2): skip every Colorado Works question
No one 60 or older: skip OAP; no one 65 or older: skip the aged Medicaid group
One person living alone: skip the relationship grid

branches: No: set every member to not pregnant (FB-03); skip pregnancy dates, expected number of children, and the pregnancy paths of MAGI, CHP+ and Colorado Works

cross_program_order.question: Does each person live in Colorado, and where: a private home, a facility (nursing facility, hospital, jail, institution), or temporarily away?
branches: Everyone in a private home in Colorado (FB-08 attestation): skip per-person settings
A person in an institution that provides most meals: that person is out of SNAP (7 CFR 273.1(b)(7)(vi)); ask the long-term care questions for Medicaid
Not in Colorado: likely not eligible for every program; still offer the application (never infer this from an unanswered question: gap G0)

gaps.title: A person who states neither a state nor a county is read as not a Colorado resident
gaps.evidence: With nothing stated, every stored af_category answer is none (71 of 71, 33 of them stored approvals), every af_oap_grant is 0 (48) and every af_and_grant is 0 (11). Under a three-valued case the same reading denies SNAP (no eligible members) and Colorado Works (residency) with no facts. Reading it as cannot determine changes none of the 3,340 stored outcome answers.
gaps.fix: derived: ["otherwise", ["=", "state_of_residence", "colorado_state_code"], ["case", [["not", ["unknown", "county_of_residence"]], true]]] (a county stated still means Colorado; neither stated is cannot determine). Until fixed, a screener must ask state or county before showing any result.

gaps.title: A first-hit case stops at the first unknown condition
gaps.evidence: Minimal denial sets hold 10312 facts with today's case and 8234 with a possible-values case (-20%). Medians, current to three-valued: SNAP 48 to 15, Colorado Works 29 to 24, CCCAP 16 to 13, MAGI 19 to 15, CHP+ 16 to 12. Of 1270 settled-but-asked facts in 307 stored denials (every value the fact can take gives a denial, yet withholding it gives cannot determine), the possible-values case settles 609. Run over the stored households it changes no settled answer; of the stored cannot-determine outcome answers, 1 becomes settled (CO-1121) and 26 become a set of possible values, one of which is a set of denials only (CO-928: residency or income).
gaps.fix: Evaluate a case to the set of values it can still produce: an unknown condition adds its arm and continues; the result is the value when every open arm agrees, else unknown (or, for = and in against a literal, settled when every possible value gives the same answer). The front end asks for the class (deny or not), not the reason, so a screener can settle "not eligible" when every open arm is a denial. A new operator semantics needs a contract version (volume.resolution.contract) and conformance cases.

gaps.title: Correlated paths: every answer leads to a denial by a different route
gaps.item: all, any, filter over unit membership
gaps.evidence: 661 settled-but-asked facts in stored denials stay unsettled under a possible-values case ({'logic': 646, 'group': 14, 'amount': 1}). Most are Colorado Works unit membership and SNAP member disqualifications: an SSI recipient or a foster child is out of the unit, and in it the unit is over income; a disqualified SNAP member is out, but the member's income still counts. Top facts: [('child_welfare_payment_type', 151), ('receives_ssi', 148), ('is_fleeing_felon', 112), ('cw_is_optional_member_by_custody_or_support', 82), ('snap_is_serving_ipv_disqualification', 23), ('snap_is_disqualified_drug_felony', 23)].
gaps.fix: What-if enumeration: for the few unanswered yes/no or one-of facts on the missing list, evaluate each value; if every value gives the same class, show "likely not eligible whatever the answer" and skip the question. Cost is 2^k evaluations; cap k at 3. An engine hook (evaluate under each value of a named fact) keeps it inside the graph.

gaps.title: Sums and groups are strict: one unknown member makes the total unknown
gaps.evidence: 14 group-membership and 1 amount cases in stored denials (more in approvals). Adult Financial already settles the resource test when the known parts exceed the limit (af_resources_known_lower_bound, CO-5350, read by af_meets_resource_limit, CO-948).
gaps.fix: Apply the CO-5350 pattern to household income tests that only add (SNAP gross, Colorado Works need standard, CCCAP and LEAP gross): a known-parts lower bound over the limit settles not eligible. Not for net income or MAGI, where deductions subtract.

gaps.title: Agency findings, referrals and claims are read bare
gaps.evidence: Every favourable path of a first-hit case must be closed before a denial settles, so the facts that open them sit in the denial sets: is_protective_services_child_care_case in 83% of stored CCCAP denials; SNAP IPV, drug-felony and work-rule findings in 85-90% of SNAP denials today (26-59% with a three-valued case); received_tanf_from_another_state_this_month in 78% of Colorado Works denials (0% three-valued).
gaps.fix: Give each finding and referral the default its own text and its rule state (no finding, not referred), as FB-04 and FB-06 propose; the agency record supplies the exceptions. They then leave the applicant interview entirely.

gaps.title: The missing-facts list depends on evaluation order
gaps.item: docs/operators.md, "Cannot determine" and its missing facts
gaps.evidence: The trace lists the unstated facts the left-to-right, short-circuit evaluation asked for. After an unknown condition stops a case, the facts that the later arms need are never listed, so a front end that asks "what is missing" learns one question at a time.
gaps.fix: With G1, list every unstated fact an open arm reads, and mark the ones whose answer can change the class. That list is the next-question set a screener needs.

gaps.title: Outcomes are per month; one answer does not settle the other months
gaps.evidence: 55 of 94 stored MAGI denials are for a month other than the determination month. Withholding the retroactive request turns 8 stored retroactive-month income denials into before-coverage-period denials (ma_month_is_before_coverage_period, CO-4101, reads an unstated request as none).
gaps.fix: Ask the months first (application date, retroactive request) and screen each month; never carry a determination-month denial to a retroactive or application month.

measured.note: questions = distinct facts asked (a household question counts once for every person); S = minimal set, current engine; Sk = minimal set, three-valued (possible-values) case; read = facts the full evaluation reads; stated = facts the stored household states. Measured with gap G0 corrected in scratch (is_colorado_resident unknown when neither state nor county is stated).

guardrails.quote: Each household has the right to file an application form on the same day it contacts the SNAP office during office hours. The household shall be advised that it does not have to be interviewed before filing the application and may file an incomplete application form as long as the form contains the applicant's name and address, and is signed by a responsible member of the household or the household's authorized representative.

Regardless of what type of application system is used, the local office must provide a means for applicants to immediately begin the application process. The household shall be advised it may file an incomplete application form if the form contains a name, address, and is signed by a responsible household member or the household's authorized representative.

If the State agency attempts to discourage households from applying for cash assistance, it shall make clear that the disadvantages and requirements of applying for cash assistance do not apply to SNAP benefits. In addition, it shall encourage applicants to continue with their application for SNAP benefits.
The eligibility site must afford any individual wishing to do so the opportunity to apply for Medical Assistance without delay.

guardrails.rule: Accept an application by every mode
guardrails.quote: the agency must accept an application from the applicant, an adult who is in the applicant's household, as defined in § 435.603(f), or family, as defined in section 36B(d)(1) of the Code, an authorized representative, or if the applicant is a minor or incapacitated, someone acting responsibly for the applicant, and any documentation required to establish eligibility
An individual shall have the opportunity to apply for Colorado Works assistance without delay.
All persons shall be provided an opportunity to file an application form on the date of initial contact with the county department during the application period.

guardrails.rule: One program does not decide another, Medicaid
guardrails.quote: If the applicant applied for Medical Assistance on the Single Streamlined Application and was found ineligible, this application shall be reviewed for all other Medical Assistance eligibility programs, the Child Health Plan Plus (CHP+) program and premium and cost-sharing assistance ... If an applicant is found to be ineligible for a particular program, the Application for Public Assistance shall be reviewed and processed for other financial programs the household has requested on the Application for Public Assistance and all other Medical Assistance Programs.

guardrails.rule: One program does not decide another, SNAP
guardrails.quote: Households applying for PA shall be notified of their right to apply for SNAP at the same time and shall be allowed to apply for SNAP at the same time they apply for PA benefits.
Review the application for completeness for all programs applied for and/or any programs not applied for but that the client is potentially eligible for.
Prior to making a determination of ineligibility, the agency must consider all bases of eligibility, consistent with § 435.911.

guardrails.rule: Retroactive months differ from the application month
guardrails.quote: An applicant does not have to be eligible in the month of application to be eligible for retroactive Medical Assistance.

guardrails.rule: SNAP benefits from the date of application
guardrails.quote: A household's benefit level for the initial months of certification shall be based on the day of the month it applies for benefits and the household shall receive benefits from the date of application to the end of the month
Missing information means "cannot determine" unless the rule says otherwise. Each supplied fact states once whether it is required or what its rule-given default is; readers do not invent defaults.
